beats.say: Minecraft never gets a final update, because it has no required goals.
The public alpha launched on 17 May 2009.
Full release arrived on 18 November 2011, yet updates kept coming.
Microsoft bought Mojang in 2014 for 2.5 billion dollars.
With no forced objectives, players shaped the world, so developers kept adding.
That open freedom meant the game could grow for over a decade without an endpoint.
That was Level Up, so subscribe for the next one. Which Minecraft update changed the game most for you?

meta.title: Level Up #3: Minecraft has no final update: here's why 🎮
meta.summary: Minecraft launched in alpha in 2009 and fully released in 2011, but its open-ended design with no required goals meant updates never needed to stop, continuing for over a decade under Microsoft.

facts: Minecraft had an initial public alpha release on 17 May 2009.
Minecraft was formally released on 18 November 2011.
Microsoft purchased Mojang and the Minecraft intellectual property in November 2014 for US$2.5 billion.
The game has no required goals, giving players a large amount of freedom in choosing how to play.
Jens "Jeb" Bergensten was handed control over development following the full release.
